turns.doctor_question: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response:
Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. I hope I'm doing this right, I've never really done this before. 

I'm here because... well, things have been really overwhelming with my house. Everyone keeps acting like this foreclosure is just, you know, regular paperwork and a few missed payments. And I really don't want to sound difficult or unreasonable—I know how it must sound to someone on the outside—but I just know that the bank, the loan servicer, and honestly even some people at my job have been quietly working together to push me out of my house. 

I mean, they keep showing me all these documents, but no amount of papers they show me changes what I’ve been seeing happening for almost two years now. Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm explaining things clearly for you, I don't want to come across the wrong way.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient expresses a fixed belief that multiple parties are conspiring to push them out of their house, which remains unchanged despite contradictory documentary evidence.

top_partial.disease_name: Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

turns.doctor_question: When you think about the bank and your job working together against you, is there any part of you that wonders whether you might be mistaken about this, or are you completely certain it's happening?

I... I really wish I could say I was mistaken. I know it would be so much easier for everyone if I was just confused about the paperwork, and I hate being the kind of person who, you know, makes a fuss or seems paranoid. I really do. 

But... no, I'm completely certain. I've been watching this happen for almost two years now. I know the bank and the loan servicer and the people at work are coordinating this. It’s just... the things I’ve seen, the way they talk to me, the timing of everything—it all lines up too perfectly to be an accident. They keep putting these foreclosure documents in front of me, trying to make it look like it's just about missed payments, but I know what's really going on underneath it all. No matter what papers they try to show me, it doesn't change the reality of what they're doing. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound crazy or stubborn to you. I just... I have to trust what I've been seeing with my own eyes, right? Is it okay that I'm being this honest with you about it?

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient expresses complete certainty that the bank and their workplace are coordinating against them, stating that no amount of contradictory evidence (paperwork) will change their belief.
